Gate and Kelvin-source traces on adjacent layers as a tight pair from the driver to the pins; driver and its decoupling within a few millimetres of the device leads, on the opposite side if the devices stand on the sink (KR-PCB-001, KR-PCB-002, KR-PCB-005, PE-PCB-001).
Both devices mounted on one shared heat sink with rated insulating pads; keep-out for pad edge creepage and mounting hardware; drain tabs at 400 V and switch-node potential (KR-TH-002, KR-ISO-002).
Provide pads for an RC snubber across the low-side device (switch node to PGND) and optionally across the input leg, populated only if double-pulse tests show ringing beyond the design margin.
Switch-node copper area limited to what current (29-32 A peak, 20.4 A RMS) and thermal spreading require, to limit dv/dt-coupled common-mode current (PE-PCB-005, PE-PCB-006, 70 um copper).

Power-board clearance/creepage for 460 V OVP working voltage and the 440 V switch node per KR-ISO-001/002 and the architecture agent's partition decision; the device choice does not depend on the partition.
open_issues: Efficiency budget: the selected 1200 V device consumes 0.83-0.93 % of the 2 % loss allowance (98 % target). If the inductor/capacitor/auxiliary budget cannot close, the documented alternatives are (a) 2 x C4MS025120K per position (-15 W), (b) C4MS018120K when stocked (-7 W), (c) 650 V C3M0015065K (-19 W) which requires reviewer acceptance of 77-84 % utilisation and a double-pulse gate V_pk <= 520 V at 440 V.

Availability: C4MS025120K shows Arrow stock only (2640) with zero at DigiKey/Richardson and a 13-week lead (search snippets, October 2026). Procurement must confirm; C3M0021120K is the pin- and gate-rail-compatible fallback (+8 W).
Short-circuit withstand time is not specified by Wolfspeed for any candidate; KR-PR-001 requires a hardware protection response <= 1.5 us (proposed) and a short-circuit test on the real device.

The 900 V class cited by the knowledge base (C3M0030090K in SKILL-006 and the TIDA-010054 analysis) is obsolete; the knowledge records need an availability note and the component database should add the C4MS family.

Design-basis suggestion: lowering the OVP trip from 460 V to about 450 V and specifying the maximum continuous input as 440 V with no switching above the trip would make the 650 V alternative defensible; with the 1200 V selection this is not needed.

Gate rails: if the architecture confirms C4MS devices only, +18 V turn-on reduces conduction loss by about 11 %; this conflicts with the C3M fallback's +19 V limit, so it must stay a BOM option (KR-GD-006).
The C4MS018120K E_rr value (720 uJ) is inconsistent with its siblings (35-256 uJ); clarify with Wolfspeed before considering it as the upgrade path.
I_D(25 degC) for C3M0032120K differs between datasheet text (69 A) and product page (63 A); not decision-relevant but recorded.
All loss figures depend on the stated scaling assumptions (+/-30 %); a double-pulse test at 400 V / 30 A with the chosen R_G values is the verification step for E_on, E_off, overshoot and dv/dt.
verification_status: Analytically checked: operating points, conduction/switching/recovery/dead-time/gate losses for 15 candidates at 400 V/25 A and six corners for the selected device and runners-up, thermal path per KR-TH-001, voltage utilisation per the stated overshoot model, paralleling comparison. All component parameters are fetched-datasheet level (Wolfspeed PDFs, revisions recorded); product status is manufacturer-page level; stock and prices are search-snippet level. Unverified: L_loop/di-dt assumptions, R_G loss factor, E(V,I) scaling, 150 degC interpolation, pad resistance, Q_G at +15 V. Human review: utilisation limits and class decision, KR-PR-001 protection timing, KR-GD-004 DESAT, KR-TH-002 pad rating, efficiency budget allocation, procurement of C4MS025120K.
markdown:
# Power semiconductor selection: Wolfspeed SiC MOSFET for the 400 V to 200 V, 5 kW, 50 kHz synchronous buck

## 1. Scope and how the knowledge base was applied

Choosing the power semiconductor is explicitly outside SKILL-001 ("Choosing the power semiconductor itself (AIPE Transistor Database scope)", SKILL-001 Not-applicable list), so no skill procedure exists for this decision. The selection below is derived from Wolfspeed datasheets (fetched PDFs, revisions listed per part) and the shared design basis; the knowledge base is applied as follows. KR-GD-001 (gate voltage within absolute maxima, hard constraint): applied directly as a selection filter and as a hand-off to the gate-driver agent. KR-TH-001 (device loss below the thermal-path limit, hard constraint): applied directly with the TIDA-010054 shared-sink model (SKILL-006 principle 1, EC-019/EC-020 pattern) but with this converter's losses, 50 degC ambient and an interface-pad assumption. KR-TH-002: applied directly (two TO-247-4 on one insulated sink is a design-basis seed). KR-PR-001 (protection faster than short-circuit withstand): surfaced as a human-review requirement because no Wolfspeed datasheet examined here states a short-circuit withstand time. KR-PCB-004 and PE-PCB-003 (commutation loop first): adapted into the loop-inductance assumption behind the overshoot estimate. REF-TI-TIDA-010054 decisions 1 and 9 (1200 V devices on an 800 V bus, 900 V devices on a 500 V bus, two TO-247 per insulated sink): adaptation evidence only (section 4). REF-WS-PRD-04814 decision 1 (+15 V / -3 to -4 V rails, +/-5 %): adapted; it is Gen-3 guidance and the Gen-4 C4MS family widens the window. SKILL-001 principles 2 and 6 (Kelvin source, C_iss/C_rss ratio) are used as selection criteria. No reference instance value (2 ohm gate resistors, 6.4 V / 1 us DESAT, 20 uF rail decoupling) is copied.

## 2. Catalog status verified on wolfspeed.com (October 2026)

- 900 V class: C3M0030090K, the TIDA-010054 500 V-side device, is marked OBSOLETE (replacements named by Wolfspeed: C3M0032120K and C4MS036120K); C3M0065090D/J are NRND. No 900 V TO-247-4 device remains, so the 900 V class is unavailable for a new design. This also means the knowledge records that cite C3M0030090K (SKILL-006, TIDA-010054 analysis) need an availability note.
- 650 V C3M (TO-247-4, T_J,max 175 degC): C3M0015065K, C3M0025065K, C3M0045065K, C3M0060065K active. C3M0030065K from the starting list does not exist.
- 1200 V C3M (TO-247-4): C3M0016120K, C3M0021120K, C3M0032120K, C3M0040120K active (175 degC); C3M0075120K active but T_J,max 150 degC.
- 1200 V Gen-4 C4MS (TO-247-4, new family): C4MS009/012/018/025/036/047/065/080120K all active; 1300 V transient rating (< 100 h lifetime), V_GS absolute -10/+23 V, drive +15 to +18 V / -5 to 0 V, T_J,max 175 degC. No Gen-4 650 V or 750 V family is listed.

## 3. Operating points (design basis, L = 267 uH)

D = Vout/Vin; dI = Vout*(1-D)/(L*fs); I_on = Io - dI/2 (high-side turn-on at the inductor valley); I_off = Io + dI/2 (high-side turn-off at the peak); I_rms,HS^2 = D*(Io^2 + dI^2/12); I_rms,LS^2 = (1-D)*(Io^2 + dI^2/12).

| Corner | D | dI (A) | I_on (A) | I_off (A) | I_rms,HS (A) | I_rms,LS (A) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 360 V / 25 A | 0.556 | 6.66 | 21.7 | 28.3 | 18.7 | 16.7 |
| 400 V / 25 A | 0.500 | 7.49 | 21.3 | 28.8 | 17.7 | 17.7 |
| 440 V / 25 A | 0.455 | 8.17 | 20.9 | 29.1 | 16.9 | 18.6 |
| 360 V / 27.5 A | 0.556 | 6.66 | 24.2 | 30.8 | 20.6 | 18.4 |
| 400 V / 27.5 A | 0.500 | 7.49 | 23.8 | 31.3 | 19.5 | 19.5 |
| 440 V / 27.5 A | 0.455 | 8.17 | 23.4 | 31.6 | 18.6 | 20.4 |

With L = 220 uH (low end of the accepted range) dI rises to 9.9 A at 440 V; the RMS values change by less than 1 %.

## 4. Voltage class, overshoot and utilisation limits

Overshoot model: V_pk = Vin + L_loop*di/dt plus ringing. Added assumptions: L_loop = 25 nH typical / 35 nH worst case for a TO-247-4 half bridge with HV ceramics beside the legs (KR-PCB-004, KR-CAP-003, PE-PCB-002/003; the two packages alone contribute roughly 10-15 nH); di/dt limited to 2.5 A/ns by R_G,off (datasheet test conditions at 1-2.5 ohm give 3.6-4.6 A/ns, so the design must slow turn-off). V_os = 25e-9 H * 2.5e9 A/s = 62 V typical, 35e-9 * 2.5e9 = 88 V worst case. The body-diode snap-off of the low-side device at high-side turn-on produces a spike of the same order on the low-side device (I_RRM about 20-30 A at the design di/dt, scaled from the datasheet I_RRM at its di_F/dt).

Utilisation limits adopted for this design: repetitive peak (including overshoot) <= 80 % of V_DS,max at 440 V; non-repetitive peak at the 460 V OVP trip <= 90 %; steady DC bus <= 70 % of V_DS,max for cosmic-ray / FIT reasons. Basis: Wolfspeed data-sheet primer "80 to 90 % of rated maximum" (search snippet), TIDA-010054 static ratios 800/1200 = 0.67 and 500/900 = 0.56 (REF-TI-TIDA-010054 decision 1), GE APEC 2015 "25 % derating for 1.2 kV SiC" (search snippet). These limits are an engineering judgement, not a Wolfspeed specification.

| Class | V_pk at 440 V (typ / worst) | utilisation | V_pk at 460 V OVP (worst) | 480 V static (100 ms) | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 650 V | 502 / 528 V | 77 / 81 % | 548 V = 84 % | 74 % | passes only with the typical loop; fails the 80 % limit at the worst-case loop and is above 80 % at the OVP corner |
| 900 V | 502 / 528 V | 56 / 59 % | 61 % | 53 % | ideal ratio, but the class is obsolete/NRND |
| 1200 V | 502 / 528 V | 42 / 44 % | 46 % | 40 % | passes with margin for any plausible layout (even 60 nH at 5 A/ns gives 740 V = 62 %) |

Why the TIDA-010054 ratios do not transfer directly: TI's 0.67 static ratio mapped to 440 V gives 657 V (a 650 V class), its 0.56 ratio gives 786 V (a 900 V class). TI's DAB is soft-switched (turn-off overshoot only, no hard reverse recovery), whereas this buck hard-switches the high side into the low-side body diode every cycle, has a 460 V OVP corner and a first-spin layout whose L_loop is unverified; and the 900 V class no longer exists. The reference ratios therefore bracket the decision but the overshoot analysis decides it: the 1200 V class is selected; the 650 V C3M0015065K is kept as the documented higher-efficiency alternative with a hard test gate (measured V_pk <= 520 V at 440 V input).

## 5. Candidate comparison at 400 V / 25 A / 50 kHz, T_J = 150 degC (typical R_DS(on))

Loss model (per device): P_cond = I_rms^2 * R_DS(on)(150 degC), with R(150) = R25 * [1 + (R_hot/R25 - 1)*(150-25)/(T_hot-25)] interpolated between the datasheet 25 degC and 175 degC (or 150 degC) typical values (C4MS: family tempco 1.88 at 175 degC; C4MS R25 taken at V_GS = 15 V). High-side switching P_sw = (E_on + E_off)*fs with E = E_ds * (Vin/V_test) * (I/I_test) * 1.3, using the body-diode-freewheeling (hottest) datasheet values, linear scaling in voltage and current, and a 1.3 factor for R_G,ext above the datasheet test value; uncertainty of this scaling is about +/-30 %. Low-side turn-on is ZVS-like (its body diode conducts during the dead time) and its turn-off commutates into its own body diode, so E_on,LS = E_off,LS = 0. Low-side reverse-recovery loss: E_rr,ds scaled (C4MS, which lists E_rr) or 0.25*Q_rr*Vin (C3M, assumption: a quarter of the swept charge is dissipated while the diode supports voltage; the remainder is already inside the high-side E_on(body diode)). Dead-time body-diode loss (LS): P_dt = t_dt*fs*V_SD,hot*(I_on + I_off) with t_dt = 250 ns per edge. E_oss is not added separately because the measured E_on already contains the C_oss energy of both devices. Gate power P_g = Q_G*19 V*fs.

Observations. The 1200 V Gen-3 parts pay a large hard-switching penalty at 400 V because their body-diode E_on (reverse recovery of the complementary device) is 3-6 times that of the 650 V parts at similar current. The Gen-4 C4MS parts cut that penalty by roughly half and have a C_iss/C_rss ratio of 630 (versus 160-400 for C3M), 1300 V transient capability and wide gate limits, at the cost of a steeper R_DS(on) tempco (1.88). Ranking by total loss: C3M0015065K 27.8 W, C3M0025065K 31.6 W, (C3M0030090K 37.4 W, obsolete), C4MS018120K 39.8 W, C4MS025120K 46.7 W, C3M0016120K 52.8 W, C3M0021120K 54.9 W, C3M0032120K 56.5 W; all others above 60 W.

## 6. Selection: Wolfspeed C4MS025120K (1200 V, 25 mohm, TO-247-4, Kelvin source), one device per position

Justification. Voltage margin: 42-44 % utilisation at 440 V including overshoot, 46 % at the 460 V OVP corner, 40 % at the 480 V survival corner, plus a 1300 V (< 100 h) transient rating; the margin absorbs any first-spin layout. Transient overshoot: the Gen-4 soft body diode (datasheet feature) and the margin above make R_G tuning a loss/EMI question rather than a survival question. Current rating: I_D = 62 A at T_C = 100 degC and 274 A pulsed against 20.4 A RMS and 31.6 A peak at the 440 V / 110 % corner; body-diode continuous 59 A. R_DS(on): 28 mohm typ at 15 V (25 mohm at 18 V), 48.5 mohm estimated at 150 degC; conduction 15.3 W per device at 400 V / 25 A. Switching energy: E_on + E_off scaled to 400 V / 21-29 A is about 151 uJ before the R_G factor, giving 9.8 W; low-side E_rr about 3.5 W. Gate charge 125 nC (at -4/+18 V, 800 V) and gate power 0.12 W per channel. Parasitic capacitances C_oss 103 pF (E_oss 63 uJ at 800 V), C_rss 4.7 pF, ratio 630 (SKILL-001 principle 6): parasitic turn-on margin is large. Package: TO-247-4 with Kelvin source (SKILL-001 principle 2, KR-PCB-003). Thermal: R_thJC 0.41 K/W; worst corner (440 V / 27.5 A) gives T_J about 104 degC (section 6.2). Availability: Arrow stock (2640, 2190 in the US) but zero at DigiKey and Richardson with a 13-week lead time, so a fallback is defined: C3M0021120K (same footprint, same +15 V / -4 V gate rails, abundant stock) accepting +8 W, or C4MS018120K (-7 W) when its stock materialises. Why not C4MS018120K as primary: datasheet Rev. 1 (June 2026), no distributor stock found, higher Q_G and its E_rr (720 uJ) is inconsistent with its siblings. Why not C3M0015065K as primary: see section 4; it remains the documented alternative if the 98 % efficiency budget cannot be closed, subject to a double-pulse overshoot gate.

### 6.2 Thermal check (KR-TH-001, KR-TH-002, SKILL-006 principle 1)

Shared heat sink 0.5 K/W at >= 2 m/s (seed), insulating pad 0.5 K/W per device (added assumption; TI's 0.1 K/W pad value is not adopted without a datasheet), R_thJC 0.41 K/W, T_A = 50 degC. Worst corner 440 V / 27.5 A: T_sink = 50 + 0.5*56.2 = 78.1 degC; T_J,HS = 78.1 + (0.5 + 0.41)*28.7 = 104.2 degC; T_J,LS = 103.2 degC; margin 46 K to the 150 degC design limit, 71 K to the device maximum. TIDA-model limit per device P_max = (150 - 50)/(2*0.5 + 0.5 + 0.41) = 52.4 W against 29.4 W worst high-side loss. The loss table is conservative (150 degC resistance), so the real junction will be lower; the thermal agent should iterate once with the actual sink.

### 6.3 One device versus two in parallel per position (400 V / 25 A, 150 degC)

C4MS025120K: 1 x 46.7 W (HS 25.1 / LS 21.6) versus 2 x 31.4 W (HS 17.4 / LS 14.0): conduction halves, E_off splits, but E_on and E_rr do not fall (doubled C_oss and Q_rr), gate charge doubles (250 nC, 0.24 W per position), four insulated TO-247-4 on the sink, and dynamic sharing depends on V_GS(th) spread (2.0-3.9 V) and symmetric Kelvin gate loops with individual R_G. The 15 W (0.3 %) gain does not justify the risk and cost at this power level (seed: one device per position), so a single device is selected; paralleling is the documented second option if the efficiency budget fails. For C3M0015065K the gain would be only 6 W (27.8 to 21.7 W).

## 7. Gate-drive requirements imposed by the selection (hand-off to the gate-driver agent)

- Rails: +15 V turn-on / -4 V turn-off, +/-5 % (KR-GD-001 check: +15.75 V and -4.2 V against C4MS limits -10/+23 V and against the C3M0021120K fallback limits -8/+19 V). C4MS alone permits +18 V (KR-GD-006 BOM option).
- Q_G = 125 nC (-4/+18 V, 800 V, 39.2 A; the +15 V / 400 V value is lower but not published): bias power 125e-9*19*50e3 = 0.12 W per channel (KR-IS-001 budget input). R_G,int = 2.6 ohm.
- Recommended external gate resistance: datasheet test 1 ohm gives t_r = 4 ns (about 200 V/ns), far too fast for CMTI and EMI. Start with R_G,on = 10-15 ohm (expected 30-60 V/ns, crude (R_ext+R_int) scaling) and R_G,off = 2-5 ohm (di/dt <= 2.5 A/ns at 29-32 A); tune by double-pulse test (SKILL-001 step 5, KR-GD-002 split outputs).
- dv/dt expectation 30-60 V/ns at turn-on: isolated driver CMTI >= 100 V/ns and isolator working voltage for a 440 V switch node (KR-SN-001). Miller immunity: C_rss*dv/dt*(R_G,off+R_G,int) = 4.7 pF * 50 V/ns * 5.6 ohm = 1.3 V above -4 V, well below V_GS(th) min 2.0 V; an active Miller clamp remains recommended (KR-GD-003).
- Peak gate current 19 V / (R_G + 2.6 ohm): 1.5 A source at 10 ohm, 3.4 A sink at 3 ohm; choose a driver with >= 4 A sink.
- Body diode: V_SD = 5.1 V (25 degC) / 4.6 V (175 degC) at 19.6 A with V_GS = -4 V; the 250 ns dead time per edge costs 2.9-3.2 W; shorter dead time is a firmware/controller option (KR-GD-009 interlock still required).
- DESAT (KR-GD-004, human review): derive the trip from the C4MS025120K output characteristics (R_DS(on) 48.5 mohm at 150 degC gives about 2.9 V at 60 A); do not reuse 6.4 V / 1 us.

## 8. Short-circuit withstand and protection speed (KR-PR-001)

No C3M or C4MS datasheet examined states a short-circuit withstand time. Wolfspeed evidence: PRD-08296 Rev. 1 (fetched) shows withstand time falling with bus voltage, 2.9 us at 800 V / 175 degC for a 1200 V module, with DESAT turn-off in about 300 ns; a Wolfspeed forum answer (search snippet) gives 9 us at 400 V and 1.8 us at 800 V for C3M0032120K at 25 degC and 15 nH. For the C4MS025120K at a 400 V bus a withstand time of several microseconds is plausible but unverified. Requirement passed to the gate-driver agent: total hardware response (blanking + detection + soft turn-off) <= 1.5 us, to be confirmed by a short-circuit test on the actual device (KR-PR-001, KR-GD-011, KR-SN-005).

## 9. Verification status

Analytically checked: operating-point currents; conduction losses with datasheet R_DS(on) and the stated temperature interpolation; switching, reverse-recovery, dead-time and gate losses with the stated scaling law; thermal path per KR-TH-001; voltage utilisation per the stated overshoot model; paralleling comparison. All datasheet parameters are from fetched Wolfspeed PDFs with revisions recorded.

Unverified: L_loop (25/35 nH) and di/dt (2.5 A/ns) assumptions; the 1.3 R_G loss factor; linear E(V, I) scaling (+/-30 %); the 25 % diode share of C3M recovery energy; R_DS(on) at 150 degC by interpolation (the datasheet curve is not digitised); Q_G at +15 V / 400 V; the 0.5 K/W pad; distributor stock and prices (search snippets, dated October 2026); C4MS018120K E_rr consistency; the C3M0032120K I_D discrepancy (69 A datasheet, 63 A product page).

Human review required: the utilisation limits (80/90/70 %) and the resulting class decision; KR-PR-001 short-circuit protection timing and test; DESAT trip and blanking (KR-GD-004); insulating pad rating and creepage on the shared sink (KR-TH-002); the 98 % efficiency budget with 0.83-0.93 % allocated to the MOSFETs (fallbacks: 650 V C3M0015065K with an overshoot test gate, or two C4MS025120K per position); procurement confirmation of C4MS025120K stock and the C3M0021120K fallback; knowledge-base update for the obsolete C3M0030090K.
